newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk Sabanci Hldg to float leading polyester unit.
newsitem.headline: Turk Sabanci Hldg to float leading polyester unit.

text.p: Sabanci Holding, one of Turkey's leading industrial conglomerates, said on Friday it would float partial share capital of its leading polyester fibre and thread producing unit in a two-day public offer next week.

"SASA (Suni ve Sentetik Elyaf Sanayii A.S.), Turkey's first and Europe's third biggest polyester producer, will be opened to public through an offer on October 23 and 24," the Holding said in a statement faxed to Reuters.

Turkey's regulatory Capital Markets Board (SPK) said in its weekly bulletin it approved the flotation of 360.5 billion lira worth of SASA shares at a fixed price of 7,200 lira per 1,000 lira nominal-valued share.
Sabanci assigned Bear, Stearns & Co Inc last November as the global lead manager and local T.Sinai Kalkinma Bankasi as the domestic lead manager for the planned offer.

The Turkish consortium led by T.Sinai Kalkinma Bankasi and co-led by T.Is Bankasi will also include seven other banks and five brokerage houses as participants while branches of Akbank, a leading commercial bank largely owned by the Sabanci group, will act as sale agents.
SASA which is also the country's sole producer of PET pellets and bottles with a recycling unit, awaits a 20 trillion lira turnover this year.
It makes around 33 percent of Turkey's total polyester fibre and thread output and is a major exporter.
Sabanci floated 15 percent of the group's giant textile subsidiary Bossa last August. Both the foreign and domestic offers of Bossa shares were oversubscribed.

Sabanci recently formed a 50-50 joint venture with German chemical group Hoechst AG to build a 145-million-mark polyester yarn and cord plant in western Turkey in reaction to growing global demand for "new generation" polyester yarns.
